_comment: Accepted findings for `npm run pii`. Everything here is a DELIBERATE decision, not a silenced alarm — each entry says who decided and why. Re-open any of them by deleting the line. The scanner derives its sensitive terms from the local machine at runtime and holds them in memory; this file is the only place an accepted identifier is written down, so keep it short and keep the reasons.
_comment_terms: Terms the scanner would otherwise flag as local machine identifiers.
_comment_terms_why: Gateway — OpenClaw product terminology ('a Gateway host may run many agents') in tools/adapters/openclaw.mjs. Fires only because a local project directory happens to share the word. Confirmed false positive by reading the context.

the-dreaming — a real local project label, published in v0.2.0 (cspace.allowlist.example.json, tools/live-server.mjs) and repeated in v0.3.0 docs and tests. Owner reviewed and ACCEPTED on 2026-08-15: it is a project name with no transcript content attached and it is already public. Retiring it would require rewriting published history.
Brad / brad-pierce — the owner's own public identity: the MIT copyright line and the GitHub handle. Explicitly accepted; the scanner flags 'Brad' only because the OS username is his first name.
_comment_patterns: Regex sources tested against the MATCHED SPAN. Used here only for INVENTED fixtures — a scanner that tests a username rule has to contain fake usernames, and a scanner that tests a private-IP rule has to contain fake IPs. Each pattern names the exact invented values rather than disabling its rule, so a REAL username, IP, MAC or address in any of those files is still caught. Deliberately not using "files" for these: tests/pii-scan.test.mjs has a self-check that scans itself and fails if the file was skipped, which is what stops this from quietly becoming a blanket exemption.
_comment_patterns_why: The invented usernames (ada, grace, mac, zaphod, pat-lee, someoneelse, ops, x) are fixtures for dehome()/compressProject() in tests/dehome.test.mjs, tests/labels.test.mjs and the doc comments in src/lib/paths.js. Zaphod and Zarquon are Hitchhiker's names, chosen so they cannot collide with a real person on this machine.
The .example TLD is RFC 2606 reserved and can never be a real address.
The three IPs and the MAC are fixtures in tests/pii-scan.test.mjs proving those rules fire. Pinned to the exact values so any OTHER private IP or MAC is still reported.
_comment_files: Paths whose findings are accepted wholesale. Keep this list as short as possible: allow-listing a FILE is much blunter than allow-listing a term, and it hides future leaks in that file too. tests/pii-scan.test.mjs is deliberately NOT here — it has a self-check that asserts its own fixtures are invented rather than real, and listing it made the scanner skip the file, turning that check into a vacuous pass.
_comment_files_why: LICENSE — the MIT copyright holder line.
_comment_reviewed: Binaries a human has ACTUALLY OPENED and cleared. A text scan cannot read pixels, so these do not pass automatically — listing one here is a claim that someone looked. Do not add a file you have not viewed.
_comment_reviewed_why: All three reviewed 2026-08-15 by frame sampling. The 35s demo video was sampled at 1 fps across its full runtime: the identity block reads DEMO-PROJECT // DEMO0000 throughout and the library panel that opens mid-reel lists only invented projects (DEMO-PROJECT, API-GATEWAY, INGEST-WORKER, SCHEMA-MIGRATE, DOCS-SITE). Re-review after any re-record.
